task.description:
Independently re-verify every REQ-358 acceptance criterion per WF-02_requirement_implementation.md Step 5 (already read) — re-run scripts/test_parallel.sh yourself (do not trust Step 4's TEST-RUNNER report alone), then check each acceptance criterion against the actual code/artefacts, not against any prior step's summary.

ONE SPECIFIC JUDGMENT CALL THIS STEP MUST MAKE, not present in a typical Step 5: Step 4b (UAT-RUNNER, handoffs/WF02-REQ358-20260916/step-04b-uat-run.json, in artifacts_in) returned PARTIAL, not PASS. Read that handoff and test/uat-reports/uat-2026-09-16-WF02-REQ358-20260916.yaml in full. Summary of what happened: (1) AC1's 'unchanged pass/fail disposition' verification against an existing scenario (loan-origination-below-threshold.yaml) came back BLOCKED — the QA instance has no Meridian tenant/fixture data seeded (real evidence quoted: GET /api/v1/identity/users?search=meridian -> {"count":0}, GET /api/v1/tenants -> only Default Tenant exists). This is a QA environment data-seeding gap, not a defect in REQ-358's schema/code — the mix task's own unit-level backward-compatibility coverage (Step 3/4, 25 tests including a live check_file/1 run against the actual unmodified Meridian file, all passing at the parse/validation level) already demonstrates the schema change is byte-for-byte non-disruptive to that exact file; what's missing is only the END-TO-END live-HTTP half, which is blocked by absent QA data, not by REQ-358. (2) AC3 (environment-target exercised for real) came back genuinely PASS — real qa-login.sh invocations, real Keycloak tokens, real distinct HTTP outcomes per role, all quoted in the report. (3) AC4 (branching sufficiency) came back PARTIAL — the branch-SELECTION mechanism was proven for real (three distinct real backend responses keyed on role), but the scenario's own steps are `via: gui` and no browser-automation tool exists yet in this pipeline, so the full GUI walkthrough leg is BLOCKED/UNBUILT_FEATURE, reported honestly rather than faked.

YOUR JOB: judge whether this constitutes 'all acceptance criteria satisfied' for REQ-358 given the above, or whether it is a genuine blocker requiring further work before DOC-UPDATER. Consider: (a) is the AC1 gap attributable to REQ-358's own implementation, or to a pre-existing QA environment limitation outside this requirement's control (check whether Meridian data was ever seeded on QA for ANY prior requirement's UAT verification, or whether QA has only ever supported platform-scope/default-tenant scenarios — this bears on whether treating the gap as 'environment, not REQ-358' is actually justified or is convenient rationalization); (b) is the AC4 GUI-leg gap similarly a pre-existing pipeline capability gap (no browser-automation tool wired in yet) rather than something REQ-358 itself needed to build (REQ-358's own SCOPE explicitly excludes 'no visual-regression mechanism' and does not promise GUI automation); (c) whether the combination of the mix task's exhaustive unit-level backward-compatibility proof (Step 3/4) plus the real API-level branch-selection proof (Step 4b) is sufficient live-system evidence for AC1/AC3/AC4's substance even though the specific literal scenario chosen (Meridian) could not complete end-to-end. State your verdict explicitly and reason through it — do not silently accept or silently reject Step 4b's PARTIAL.

If you conclude these gaps are pre-existing/out-of-REQ-358's-control and the evidence gathered is substantively sufficient: PASS, route to DOC-UPDATER, and name the two gaps (QA Meridian data absence; no browser-automation tool) as fast-follow items for RELEASE-VALIDATOR's own record, not silently dropped. If you conclude otherwise: FAIL with the specific blocking gap named and which agent it routes back to.
